issues.legal_issue: In an agricultural income-tax assessment of tea income, the state assessor must use a prior central computation where the state law adopts that computation and does not authorize the assessor to disregard it.
material_facts: The taxpayers cultivated, manufactured and sold tea, and the central income-tax authorities computed their tea income before the agricultural income-tax assessments were made.
The taxpayers provided the central assessment orders and asked the agricultural income-tax officer to use the computed agricultural portion of the tea income.
The officer instead made an independent computation, producing a higher agricultural income figure.

The state law defined agricultural income from tea by reference to the central income-tax computation and did not authorize the officer to disregard a computation already made by the central authorities.
issues.conclusion: The agricultural income-tax officer was bound to accept the prior central computation and assess only the agricultural portion of that computation, less allowable deductions not already granted.
issues.legal_principle: The constitutional division of taxing powers, including Articles 274(1) and 366 and Entries 46 of List II and 82 of List I, confines state taxation to agricultural income as defined for income-tax purposes. Under section 10 and rule 24 of the Income-tax Act, 1922 and Rules, and the corresponding provisions of the 1961 Act and rule 8, tea income is computed as business income and apportioned between non-agricultural and agricultural income. The explanation to section 2(a)(2) and section 5 of the Kerala Agricultural Income-tax Act adopt that computation, subject to allowable deductions not already made; section 6 and rule 15 govern apportionment for land partly within and partly outside the state. Karimtharuvi Tea Estates Ltd. v. State of Kerala, [1963] Supp. 1 SCR 823, was followed, and Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax, Kerala v. Perunad Plantations Ltd., (1965) 56 ITR 193, was overruled. The decision does not establish that a central computation under rule 23 or rule 7 is binding.

predicates.tea_agricultural_income_assessment: The proceeding assesses the agricultural portion of income from tea that the taxpayer cultivated, manufactured and sold.
predicates.central_computation_completed_before_sta: The central tax authority completed its computation of the tea income before the state assessor began the agricultural income-tax assessment.
predicates.state_law_adopts_central_computation: The governing state law defines the agricultural portion of tea income by reference to the central computation.
predicates.state_law_confers_no_power_to_disregard_: The governing state law gives the state assessor no authority to disregard a central computation already completed.

issues.definition: When an agricultural income-tax assessment concerns tea income, the central computation was completed first, the state law adopts it and that law gives the state assessor no power to disregard it, the state assessor must use that computation.

issues.legal_issue: A surcharge on agricultural income cannot be levied for an assessment year in which the applicable surcharge law does not authorize it.
material_facts: In some assessments, the agricultural income-tax officer imposed a surcharge of five per cent on agricultural income for the assessment year 1957-58.
The Court had previously held that no surcharge on agricultural income could be levied under the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, for that assessment year.
issues.conclusion: The surcharge could not be levied on agricultural income for the assessment year 1957-58.
issues.legal_principle: Karimtharuvi Tea Estate Ltd. v. State of Kerala, [1966] 3 SCR 93; [1965] 60 ITR 262, held that the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 did not permit a surcharge on agricultural income for the assessment year 1957-58. That ruling was followed.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding assesses income treated as agricultural income for tax purposes.
predicates.surcharge_imposed_on_agricultural_income: The assessor imposed a surcharge on the agricultural income being assessed.
predicates.assessment_year_not_subject_to_surcharge: The applicable surcharge law, as interpreted by the court, does not authorize a surcharge for the assessment year in question.

issues.definition: When an agricultural income-tax assessment includes an imposed surcharge and the applicable law does not authorize a surcharge for that assessment year, the surcharge is not leviable.
